title: Fried Chicken in a Pan – The Food & Wine Winner
description: Food & Wine readers also love fried chicken, and the magazine’s archive offers no shortage of recipes. A panel of editors, alongside experts from the Food & Wine Test Kitchen, selected six recipes from famous chefs and culinary professionals. Each recipe was tested and tasted — a happy day for the team. The buffet of fried chicken options sparked lively conversation about how to achieve the crispiest breading and juiciest meat. But one recipe delighted us most of all, and it was also one of the easiest to make: Winner: Super-Crispy Pan-Fried Chicken , by Angie Mosier, an Atlanta cook, writer, photographer, and stylist.
ingredients: 8 pieces of chicken (preferably drumsticks and thighs)
¾ quarts vegetable oil, for frying
directions: In a large bowl, toss the chicken with the buttermilk. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate the chicken for at least 8 hours or overnight.

In a large, resealable plastic bag, combine the flour, salt, pepper, and cayenne. Set two large racks over rimmed baking sheets. Working in batches, drain the chicken, scraping off most of the buttermilk against the side of the bowl.
Add the chicken to the bag, a few pieces at a time, and shake to coat completely. Transfer the chicken to the racks, pressing the flour to help it adhere as you remove the chicken from the bag.

Pour 1 inch of oil into each of two large cast-iron skillets and heat to 350°F. Add about half of the chicken pieces to the hot oil, being sure not to crowd the skillet. Fry over moderate heat until the chicken is golden, crisp, and cooked through, 20 to 25 minutes; an instant-read thermometer should register 165°F for thighs or drumsticks and 160°F for breasts.
Line the racks with paper towels and drain the chicken. Continue frying the chicken in batches, being sure the oil temperature stays at 325°F during frying. Serve warm or at room temperature.
